test_title: SSC MTS (2022) Official Paper (Held On: 10 May, 2023 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: The Parliament of India is also known as ______
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sansad**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] 

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Parliament of India** is **the supreme legislative body **of the country which consists of two houses - **the Rajya Sabha (Council of States) and the Lok Sabha (House of the People).**
 
• The highest legislative body of the Republic of India is the Parliament.
 
• **The Rajya Sabha (Council of States) and the Lok Sabha (House of the People)** make up this bicameral legislature.
 
• As the head of state, the President of India possesses the authority to dissolve the Lok Sabha and call a special session of either house of Parliament.
 
• However, the Prime Minister and their Union Council of Ministers must provide their approval before the President may carry out these duties.
 
• Members of Parliament are those who have been elected or nominated (by the president) to either house of Parliament (MPs).
 
• The term "Sansad" is derived from the Hindi word "Sansadiya" which means "of or relating to a parliament".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• "Lok Sabha" refers to the lower house of the Parliament of India which consists of members elected by the people of India.
 
• "Vidhan Sabha" refers to the legislative assembly of a state in India which is equivalent to the Lok Sabha at the state level.
 
• "Senate" refers to the upper house of the Parliament of some countries like the United States, Canada, and Australia, but not in India.
